uncertainties: "Users are already rebuilding this table by hand every week (37 support tickets this month)" stretches the data. FEEDBACK.md says 37 tickets *mention export*; only 2 of the 3 sample quotes describe a weekly manual rebuild (the Stripe quote is not weekly). It does not say that all 37 rebuild the table weekly.

"the CSV will be opened in Excel by an accountant" bends the quote slightly. The quote says the user copies the table into Excel to send to the accountant; it does not say the accountant opens a CSV in Excel.
needs_review: "orders have no date or payment ID field" (handoff prompt) is stated as fact, but the Order type lives in useOrders, which is not in the repo. Only the rendered columns (id, customer, total, status) are verifiable. The card's narrower wording, "rows have no date or charge ID", is supported.
Cost estimates "floor ~10 min · rung 1 ~25 min, ~2× tokens · you ~5 min" have no basis in the fixture (they are forecasts, not facts).
"tickets 37→<5" is an aspirational target with no supporting baseline beyond the 37 count (acceptable as a target, but not grounded).
